title: #4471 review · separate parser and booking-hint failures · support kb
text:
support desk · kb
#4471 review · separate parser and booking-hint failures

owner Grzegorz Ludwa and Codex harness
reviewed
reviewed 2026-10-28 · 0 days ago

Reports merged into #4471 cover distinct parser and booking-hint failures. Keep a ticket for each cause: fixing the shared parser does not correct the booking form’s misleading hint. This review replaces the one issue, one fix conclusion in the original incident account; that account remains as the historical record.

Public follow-up tickets
Parser failure · follow-up issue 1
Booking-hint failure · follow-up issue 2

These issue numbers belong to the public follow-up repository. The table below shows the source desk’s routing in the supplied export, including reports it had not given their own ticket.

What the running views show

412 reports merged into #4471 · 2 causes

cause	reports	tagged as	tenants	seen	
parser	379	parser ×356 · hint ×23	11	2026-04-01 → 2026-10-04	#4471
hint	33	hint ×18 · parser ×15	3	2026-04-17 → 2026-09-22	not this ticket — no ticket of its own

5 reports read as a one-day move; filed under parser by tenant.

These counts come from the current report data at render time. The component first removes overlapping export rows by report ID, then groups reports by causeOf using the tenant’s directory entry. It does not group by subject, browser locale, or meta.intakeTag. The original ticket belongs to the largest cause group; the other cause needs its own ticket. The public tickets record counts for the supplied export, not a promise that future counts stay fixed.

Parser

The shared parser reads month first, although the affected tenants write day first. App and email reports belong here, as do form reports whose tenant uses booking-v2. For example, R-41200 reports 7 April becoming 4 July for Harbour Dental (en-GB). The expected behavior is to interpret the date using the tenant’s date convention. Check the shared parser with an unambiguous day above twelve and an ambiguous day/month pair; no product runtime was supplied, so these are verification scenarios rather than executed product tests.

Booking hint

For a day-first tenant using booking-v3, a form-channel report belongs to hint: the field prints MM/DD/YYYY, but the form reads the date in the tenant’s day-first order. People following the displayed hint can therefore submit a different date from the one intended. For example, R-41241 is an Alder Physio form report (de-DE, booking-v3), while an app report from the same tenant still belongs to parser. Make the hint agree with the form’s interpretation and verify a date entered exactly as instructed. Do not close this ticket merely because the shared parser is fixed.

Some reports describe a one-day move. The desk's exception list is footnoted in the live cause table and stays inside its assigned group. Those descriptions deserve follow-up; they do not establish another cause or justify counting a report twice.

Received dates and merge dates answer different questions. The large merge batch is not the start of the incident. Reports continue after that batch: a known ticket and a queued fix are not evidence that the problem stopped. Keep the receipt and merge timelines separate.

How to handle the next report
Find the tenant’s locale and booking-form version in the directory. Browser locale is an intake hint.
Apply causeOf from src/lib/kb/causes.ts using the report channel and that tenant entry.
Merge only when sameCause confirms the same non-null cause. Matching subjects are insufficient; different subjects can still describe the same cause.
If the tenant is missing or the cause is null, leave the report unplaced for investigation.
Deduplicate export overlaps by ID before counting, and retain the report IDs behind each ticket.

The prose in the old triage guide follows accepted decision 0001, while its explorer runs the cause rules. Their disagreement matters: the decision and triage text were last reviewed in 2024. Preserve the accepted decision; the desk should supersede it with a new decision before treating the revised general policy as accepted. This review provides the incident-specific rule.

Provenance and limits

Source: the support kb export dated 2026-10-04, including reports-4471.json, the tenant directory, desk-notes.json, and the executable views in src/lib/kb/. The classifications are the supplied desk rules, not an independently confirmed diagnosis of a running production system. Preserve the original data and re-render after updates. Use the repository’s evidence/report-groups.json for the report IDs and drafts/ for the corresponding ticket text.
